title: Monotonicity of nondeterministic acceptance
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet, let $x$ be a binary string, and let $t,t'\in\mathbb{N}$ with $t\le t'$. If some choice word of length exactly $t$ leads $N$ on input $x$ to a halted configuration whose output is the one-bit string $1$, then some choice word of length exactly $t'$ does so as well.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over the binary alphabet
Some length-$t$ choice word leads to a halted configuration with output exactly $[1]$
replaced:
Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic multi-tape Turing machine over the binary
alphabet, let $x$ be a binary string, and let $t \le t'$ be natural numbers. If some
choice word of length $t$ drives $N$ on input $x$ to a halted configuration with output
exactly $1$, then some choice word of length $t'$ does as well; that is, if $N$ accepts
$x$ within $t$ steps then $N$ accepts $x$ within $t'$ steps.
